claim: Settle commit hygiene for concurrently-written graph repos: a mid-session commit that stages the graph file sweeps foreign in-flight writes and can land a torn HEAD where the repo's own gates are red. Decide and encode the rule - for example, run the repo gates (mix cb.verify.schema, mix cb.generate.claude_md --check) against the staged tree before any commit touching graph-rendered surfaces, or coordinate commits across live sessions.

evidence.detail: First specimen, 585f9ec: a session minting b535/b536 staged beliefs.json while the b531 ceremony was mid-flight in another session, committing the b533/b065 supersessions and t0019 materialization without the matching regenerated CLAUDE.md - at that commit mix cb.generate.claude_md --check fails. No data lost in either direction; the b531 close's commit repairs main. The hazard is structural: CLAUDE.md's own session-start doctrine says other sessions write these repos concurrently, so selective staging of a shared graph file will recur. Preflight 2026-06-12 under the b064 calibration: 0 contract, 0 schema, 29 neutral; the single claim_overlap was b450 (the verify-tooling line this directive asks to invoke at commit time), supportive in spirit, reviewed per b055.

Second specimen, 2026-06-23: a session staged beliefs.json carrying its cb:b550/cb:b551 stale-reference fix (the b043->b066 cascade) after running mix bs stale --cascade (clean) and mix cb.verify.schema (green). Before it ran git commit, a concurrent session's commit (8c161cf, minting cb:b549) had already staged the same beliefs.json and swept the b550/b551 writes into its own commit and push - so the agent's own 'git commit' found nothing to commit and a clean tree. The agent verified b550/b551 were present in HEAD and on origin (they were), so nothing was lost this time. Unlike the 585f9ec specimen the swept HEAD was gates-green, but only by timing luck, not because the committing session checked: the sweep mechanism is identical and the torn-HEAD risk b538 names is unmitigated.

Mitigation landed 2026-07-06: the per-belief split (cb:b554/b558) dissolves the sweep mechanism for non-overlapping writes - concurrent sessions minting different nodes stage disjoint beliefs/cb/<local>.json files, so a mid-session commit no longer scoops a foreign in-flight write out of a shared array file. The torn-HEAD hazard narrows to genuinely overlapping writes to the same node and to shared rendered surfaces (CLAUDE.md); the gates-before-commit discipline this item asks to encode remains undecided.
